text.title: Cognitive Walkthrough: Basics Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the question is first-use learnability at all, whether a single correct sequence and a per-state interface exist to walk, and how answers are being recorded — to the four-question inspection, a prerequisite fix, or a skip to moderated usability testing.

decision-tree.root-question: What is being asked about the interface — how quickly a user gets through it, or whether a first-time user can work it out at all?

branch.when: the question is task time, error rate, efficiency or satisfaction for users who already know the product

conclusion.verdict: skip: those measures need observed users and a walkthrough has none — route to moderated usability testing, where task performance is actually measured

branch.when: every real user is trained, onboarded or a repeat user, so no first encounter exists in the population

conclusion.verdict: skip: the method simulates a first-time exploratory user; with no such user the findings describe nobody — run a usability test with the trained population instead

branch.when: the question is whether a first-time user can work the interface out without training
branch.question: Can one correct action sequence be written down, and is each interface state visible after each action?

branch.when: the task is open browsing or an exploratory dashboard with no single correct sequence

conclusion.verdict: skip: without a definable correct sequence, Q2 and Q4 have nothing to inspect and the session degenerates into design critique wearing walkthrough formatting

branch.when: a sequence exists but the only artefact is a feature list or a boxes-and-arrows flow diagram with no per-state interface

conclusion.verdict: skip until at least labelled wireframes show the state after each action — a feature list is below the minimum the method needs

branch.when: a linear correct sequence and per-state screens exist, but the simulated user is described only as a new user

conclusion.verdict: write the persona first: the domain vocabulary they use, comparable products they have used, and what they do not know — otherwise evaluators substitute their own wording and every product-internal term passes Q3

branch.when: a linear correct sequence, per-state screens and a persona with stated vocabulary are all in hand

conclusion.verdict: apply the full inspection: freeze `correct_steps`, then answer all four questions per step with yes/no plus a reason, and a failure story behind every no

branch.when: a walkthrough is under way and the open question is how to record what is being found
branch.question: What is happening to the record as the steps are walked?

branch.when: a better path was noticed mid-walk and the temptation is to substitute it into the sequence

conclusion.verdict: log the better path as an issue and keep walking the frozen sequence; swapping paths deletes the failing steps and ends with a clean report of a route no first-time user would take

branch.when: no answers are being recorded as verdicts — the label is unclear — with no account of what the user would believe and do next

conclusion.verdict: write the failure story or drop the finding: the fix is derivable from the wrong belief, not from the verdict

branch.when: severity is being expressed as percent of users affected, frequency, or frequency times impact

conclusion.verdict: re-rate on the blocking scale — blocker, detour, hesitation; any percentage here is a fabricated number that will later be quoted as measurement

branch.when: a blocker was found at an early step and later-step findings are being reported as independently confirmed

conclusion.verdict: mark every finding after the blocker as conditional and re-walk the tail once the blocker is fixed — those steps describe a state no current user can reach
